title: 6 reps. 12 reps. 25 reps. Same muscle group, about 10 seconds between lifts.
hook: 6 reps. 12 reps. 25 reps. Same muscle group, about 10 seconds between lifts.
caption:
6 reps. 12 reps. 25 reps. Same muscle group, about 10 seconds between lifts.

This is Charles Poliquin’s 6-12-25 method, and it’s still one of my favorite plateau breakers.

How it works
The 6: heavy compound, 4-0-1-0 tempo. Seated DB shoulder press.
The 12: second compound from a new angle, 3-0-1-0. Low-incline DB press.
The 25: lighter load, steady rhythm, 2-0-1-0. Flat DB press.
Rest 2 to 3 min. Repeat for 2 to 3 rounds.

title: Muscle growth isn’t just about moving weight. It’s about creating enough mechanical tension to challenge your muscles and stimulate adaptation.
hook: Muscle growth isn’t just about moving weight. It’s about creating enough mechanical tension to challenge your muscles and stimulate adaptation.
caption:
Muscle growth isn’t just about moving weight. It’s about creating enough mechanical tension to challenge your muscles and stimulate adaptation. 

Train with purpose, not just effort.

Mechanical tension is the force experienced by muscle fibers when they contract against resistance. 

It’s a primary stimulus for hypertrophy. The goal isn’t simply to lift weight, but to make your muscles work hard against it.

Your muscles should be doing the work not gravity or momentum 

Challenging resistance creates tension within muscle fibers, triggering signals that support growth.

title: Ever finished a set and thought, “I didn’t really feel that… did it even work?” 🤔
hook: Ever finished a set and thought, “I didn’t really feel that… did it even work?” 🤔
caption:
Ever finished a set and thought, “I didn’t really feel that… did it even work?” 🤔

It’s a common thought, but not feeling a strong burn doesn’t mean the exercise wasn’t effective.

Mind-muscle connection can be useful, particularly with isolation exercises, but technique, range of motion, effort, and progression matter more. 💪

So instead of chasing a burn, focus on whether you’re performing the movement well and improving over time.
